text:
Father Noah, who planted vines, and you, Lot, who drank so much in the cave that Love, ever full of traps, made you “know” your girls—not reproach, sweet innocent—and Architriclinus, certified drunkard, I pray you welcome grandly the soul of good Cotart, deceased.

Born long ago of your lineage, he drank the dearest and finest and excelled all at not paying. A bold knight of wine, he never trembled climbing barrels and fiercely defended his glass. Open Paradise's gates to the soul of good Cotart, deceased.

How often I saw the reveler stagger off to bed! Once he raised a bump striking a master butcher's stall. I doubt the world holds a man more enamored of wine. Let it enter when you hear it complain, the soul of good Cotart, deceased.

His spit never reached the ground. He cried, “My throat is on fire!” His soul could never quench its thirst, the soul of good Cotart, deceased.
